request.text:
\(A_1\cap B_2\) and \(A_2\cap B_1\) are signed-null.
The partition itself need not be unique: by
\cref{thm:p15-w02b-p15-005-hahn-partitions}, the Hahn partitions are
exactly the signed-null modifications of one of them, and the partition is
unique exactly when the empty set is the only signed-null set.
\Cref{thm:p15-w02b-p15-005-density-hahn} gives the source's description
of the Hahn positive sets of an integral-defined signed measure and three
distinct ones on the unit interval.
request.reason: ED26-P15-CH-radon-nikodym-C006: the host asserts non-uniqueness of the Hahn partition without witness. The exact characterization, the source's {f>0} subset A subset {f>=0} a.e. variant (Durrett printed p. 468) and a concrete witness are proved in handbook/parts/p15/measure-integration-and-product-constructions-w02b-p15-005.tex with annex proofs in handbook/annex/p15/measure-integration-and-product-constructions-w02b-p15-005.tex.

request.anchor_quote:
Their individual Stieltjes measures need not already be the mutually
singular Jordan components.
request.text:
Their individual Stieltjes measures need not already be the mutually
singular Jordan components. For instance, if \(F\) is any such function
that is not identically zero and \(G=F\), the represented signed measure
is zero, so both Jordan components vanish, while \(\mu_F=\mu_G\) is a
nonzero measure. In general, by \cref{thm:p15-w02b-p15-005-stieltjes-excess},
the two Stieltjes measures exceed the Jordan components by one common
finite measure, which vanishes exactly when they are mutually singular.
request.reason: ED26-P15-CH-radon-nikodym-C009: the host asserts that the Stieltjes measures of F and G need not be the Jordan components without witness or argument. The common-excess theorem, its equivalence with mutual singularity and the F=G witness are proved in handbook/parts/p15/measure-integration-and-product-constructions-w02b-p15-005.tex with annex proofs in handbook/annex/p15/measure-integration-and-product-constructions-w02b-p15-005.tex. The replacement text states the F=G witness inline (proved as part (6) of that theorem) so the host assertion carries its own witness.
